newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Senate calls for end to embargo on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Senate calls for end to embargo on Iraq.

text.p: The Italian Senate approved a motion on Tuesday aimed at revoking the international economic embargo on Iraq and releasing Iraqi assets held in Italian and other foreign banks.

The motion, which still needs approval from the lower house, would commit the Italian government to push for a gradual end to the embargo, imposed by the United Nations after Iraq's 1991 invasion of Kuwait.
The government would also be required to verify whether Iraqi assets frozen in Italian banks can be released and used to provide food and medicine for the Iraqi people.
Italy would call on other U.N. member states to do the same, according to the motion.
In a second motion approved on Tuesday by the Senate, the government would pledge to support organisations working to guarantee civil rights in Iraq.
The two motions were submitted by senators from both government and opposition parties and won a large majority, with abstentions only by senators from the separatist Northern League party.
